Read a published Python 1.2 scientific-result JSON and NPZ snapshot in native R

etr_read_python_portable_result.Rd

Reads eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 export_portable_result() bundles in R without executing Python. Validates the schema, SHA-256 checksum and NumPy archive entries, then reconstructs the supported safe scientific arrays, tables, mappings and dataclass-field snapshots. This is an explicitly limited native reader; it does not claim a complete replacement for Python's load_portable_result() or serve as a Python-format writer.

Usage

etr_read_python_portable_result(directory,
  max_array_bytes = 64 * 1024^2,
  max_total_bytes = 128 * 1024^2)

Arguments

directory

Directory containing the published Python v1 manifest.json and arrays.npz files.

max_array_bytes

Finite positive byte cap (at least 1024 and at most 1 GiB) for each decoded numeric/Unicode array. Defaults to 64 MiB.

max_total_bytes

Finite positive byte cap on the total advertised uncompressed archive entries. Defaults to 128 MiB.

Value

An etr_python_portable_snapshot R list with result_type, source_package_version, payload, units, environment, nonportable_fields, arrays_sha256, archive_keys and the original manifest.

Python dataclasses become R named lists with a __python_type__ field, not executable or refitted objects. Python tuples become lists of class etr_python_tuple. Native R data.frames may carry an additional python_index attribute. R NA/NaN values are preserved in decoded arrays.

Details

This function has no Python dependency. Only the optional R packages jsonlite and digest are needed at call time. The checksum verifies arrays.npz before parsing; the Python manifest itself is not cryptographically signed. Provenance/source authenticity is not thereby established.

The loader accepts the published version-one Python format with the exact arrays.npz filename, including array-free snapshots, and bounds uncompressed size. It reads safe NumPy NPY v1-v3 little-endian binary arrays using a typed subset of floating, integer, bool and UTF-32 Unicode descriptors, and primitive homogeneous JSON-backed object arrays. JSON nulls become missing values of the observed type. If every cell is null, the snapshot carries logical missing values because the source has no element type information. Signed and unsigned 64-bit integers must be within the inclusive exact integer range of base R doubles. Embedded NUL characters in Unicode arrays are rejected because R strings cannot represent them. Pickling or backend execution is never attempted. Unsupported dtypes, heterogeneous object arrays, irregular table schemas and unknown markers fail closed instead of silently discarding scientific state.

It is read-only; the Stage 5 native R snapshot format is different and is not exchanged through this function. The published Python portable writer stores backend-native objects as explicit nonportable markers and its loader does not reconstruct fitted estimator objects. Equivalent native-R fitted-estimator reconstruction is not offered here.

The reader imposes explicit byte caps, dtype restrictions and representation limitations not imposed identically by upstream Python. It is therefore an independently implemented partial public function candidate, not proof of exact one-to-one general contract equivalence or scientific inference qualification.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Requires a previously exported trusted Python 1.2 portable bundle:
snapshot <- etr_read_python_portable_result("path/to/portable_export")
str(snapshot$payload)
} # }
